title: Cliff's Village years, radio broadcasts and recordings
summary: He played Terrasi's and Gondon's, was broadcast, and made a Harlem Banjo album in the 1950s.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Yeah, before he went into Cafe Society he was very popular in the Village, he worked at a place -- Nick's in the Village, it was quite a musicians hangout and he and Pee Wee Russell were very good friends. I think he made some records, probably a set of 78's and an album with Pee Wee Russell which I don't have at the present time. This was before, you know, cliff and I got together. But there are some photos around the house that were taken during the session, but I don't happen to have a copy of that album.
But when he was working -- there might

be a lot of stuff at the house on tape of Cliff's because he had a lot of friends and they sent him a lot of stuff, which I haven't heard because it's reel to reel and I don't have the equipment. In those days I guess we had an early wire recorder. You remember the wire recorder?
I know of them, it was a bit before my time.

Yeah, right, but anyway, they used to broadcast from Terrasi's and he'd go to work at night and we'd set up the recorder and take some of the stuff off the air. So I probably have a lot of stuff at home that I just haven't had a chance to hear that Cliff made live from wherever he was working, especially if he had remote broadcasting.

Well, he made an album, as I told you before, the Harlem Banjo album, with Elmer Snowden. This was made in Englewood Cliffs. Luckily enough, a friend of mine gave me a copy of that album, but you can't find it anywhere now. Then he did -- there's a couple solos of his on an album,

That's the same one where you appeared in 1956.

And then just before he passed, Fat Cat arranged for him to make an album, solo piano and it's called "Parlor Piano," I think and it came out the day that he passed. Of course this was taken later in his career. In fact he had had a couple heart attacks before that, before the album was made and he wasn't exactly up to par, as well as, you know, he would like to have been because he had been quite seriously ill. But that's the last album that he made.
